references.text: The Lord's cloud and pillar of fire guided the people of Israel day and night during their exodus from Egypt, demonstrating God's continuous leadership over His people.
The cloud above the tabernacle signaled when the Israelites should break camp and move on, and it was over them throughout all their journeys.
A detailed description of how the cloud covered the tabernacle and led the people when they were to travel or set up camp.
It mentions that the Lord went before the people in a pillar of cloud by day, confirming God's visible presence and guidance.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord went before them on the way by night in fire and by day in a cloud.
The cloud filled the Lord's house at the temple dedication, showing God's glorious presence in the form of a cloud also within the temple.
The psalm describes how God led the people with a cloud by day and with a pillar of fire throughout the night.
God spread out a cloud as a covering for the people, a poetic rendering of the cloud's protective function.
The prophecy that the Lord will create a cloud by day over Mount Zion, pointing back to the cloud of the wilderness wanderings.
Paul refers to the fact that all their fathers were under the cloud, serving as a typology for baptism and God's guidance.
